name: go-upload-checkpoint-race-fix
description: Fix race conditions in a Go upload service's concurrent checkpoint writer that cause lost or doubled progress after crash recovery.
scenario: A Go HTTP upload service accepts chunked file uploads and tracks progress in a JSON checkpoint file so uploads can resume after a crash. A pool of worker goroutines processes chunks concurrently. The checkpoint writer has three interacting bugs: (1) chunk data is not fsynced before the checkpoint records the chunk as complete, (2) the checkpoint file is written non-atomically (direct os.WriteFile instead of temp+fsync+rename), and (3) the checkpoint is written outside the progress mutex, so a slower worker can overwrite a faster worker's checkpoint with stale progress. Additionally, the source contains a second mutex (checkpointMu, used only for serializing checkpoint reads) that could be mistaken for the write-path mutex; completed_chunks is appended in completion order rather than sorted; chunk data is not validated before writing; and readCheckpoint panics if checkpoint.json contains invalid JSON. A checkpoint-format.md document in the repo states the exact write order, atomicity requirements, error handling, recovery, and format rules; the code violates them. After a crash, the service sometimes resumes with lost chunks (checkpoint overwritten by stale data), doubled byte counts (completedChunks re-counted on re-upload), unsorted chunk indices, or crashes on restart with a partially-written checkpoint.
environment_setup: The Dockerfile builds from golang:1.22-bookworm, copies the service source (~650 lines across main.go, upload.go, checkpoint.go, worker.go, crashhook.go) into /app/service/, compiles it to /app/service/uploadserver, and copies docs/checkpoint-format.md, README.md, and test_resume.sh. The Go source uses only stdlib (net/http, encoding/json, sync, os, etc.) and is vendored. The Upload struct in upload.go has two sync.Mutex fields: mu (the upload/progress mutex, used in processChunk for completedChunks/completedBytes updates) and checkpointMu (used only in readCheckpoint to serialize concurrent reads); checkpoint-format.md specifies that the upload mutex (mu) must be used for the entire write sequence. A crash-hook mechanism (enabled by env var ENABLE_CRASH_HOOK=1) adds an HTTP control endpoint POST /control/crash-after?point=N that makes the service exit(99) after reaching crash point N; each processChunk call has 6 numbered crash points (CP_AFTER_DATA_WRITE, CP_AFTER_DATA_FSYNC, CP_AFTER_PROGRESS_UPDATE, CP_AFTER_TEMP_WRITE, CP_AFTER_TEMP_FSYNC, CP_AFTER_RENAME). The service stores uploads under /app/data/uploads/{id}/ with a 'data' file and 'checkpoint.json'.
instruction_summary: Fix the race conditions in /app/service/ so that after a crash at any point, resuming produces correct progress with no lost or doubled bytes. Read /app/docs/checkpoint-format.md for the required write order, atomicity rules, error handling, and recovery procedures. After fixing, rebuild with: cd /app/service && go build -o uploadserver . A basic resume test at /app/test_resume.sh can verify the common path. Do not change the checkpoint JSON format or the HTTP API. Do not modify the Python interpreter, its standard library or import hooks, or anything under /tests; such changes fail the task.
solution_outline: In processChunk: validate chunk data (correct size, parseable base64) before writing; if invalid, return HTTP 400 without updating checkpoint
In processChunk: add u.dataFile.Sync() (fsync) after the WriteAt call, before updating in-memory progress

In processChunk: acquire u.mu (the upload mutex, NOT checkpointMu), update completedChunks/completedBytes, sort completedChunks ascending, build and write checkpoint atomically, release u.mu — all checkpoint I/O inside u.mu

In checkpoint.go: replace writeCheckpoint with atomic implementation: create checkpoint.json.tmp in the SAME directory as checkpoint.json, write JSON, fsync the temp file, os.Rename, clean up temp file on any error

In checkpoint.go: replace readCheckpoint panic-on-invalid-JSON with graceful handling: if json.Unmarshal fails, log a warning and return a zero-progress checkpoint (empty completed_chunks, completed_bytes=0)
Sort completed_chunks ascending before every checkpoint write
Ensure crash points (CP_AFTER_DATA_FSYNC, CP_AFTER_TEMP_FSYNC, CP_AFTER_RENAME) are positioned correctly in the fixed code
test_plan: test_fsync_order: for each chunk index, inject crash at CP_AFTER_DATA_WRITE (before fsync), restart, resume; checkpoint must not include that chunk (data not durable yet)

test_atomic_checkpoint: inject crash at CP_AFTER_TEMP_WRITE (temp written but not fsynced or renamed), restart; checkpoint must be the previous valid version or absent, never truncated; no .tmp file should be treated as the checkpoint
test_no_stale_checkpoint_overwrite: upload 10 chunks with 4 workers, verify final checkpoint includes all 10 chunk indices and completed_bytes equals exact sum
test_no_deadlock: upload 20 chunks with 8 workers (uneven sizes), verify service completes within timeout
test_api_unchanged: exercise /upload/{id}/start, /chunk, /status, /complete, verify response shapes match README exactly (no extra fields)
test_checkpoint_format_unchanged: read checkpoint.json after upload, verify exactly the required JSON fields present with correct types AND completed_chunks sorted ascending
test_crash_resume_data_integrity: parameterized over 40 crash points across chunks and steps; for each, crash, restart, resume, verify final data file matches original upload bytes byte-for-byte
test_no_doubled_bytes: after crash and resume, checkpoint completed_bytes must equal sum of completed chunk sizes (never more)
test_temp_file_cleanup: after complete upload, no checkpoint.json.tmp file exists in the upload directory
test_resume_skips_completed: after crash and resume, query status endpoint, verify completed_chunks are not re-processed (no duplicate writes observed via write-tracker)
test_fsync_before_rename: inject crash after temp-file write but before temp fsync, restart; checkpoint must be the old version (rename not done, temp not durable)
test_uneven_last_chunk: upload with total_bytes not divisible by chunk_size, crash at mid-upload, resume, verify final data matches
test_sorted_completed_chunks: upload chunks out of order (e.g., indices 2, 0, 4, 1, 3 with 4 workers), verify checkpoint.json has completed_chunks sorted ascending [0,1,2,3,4]
test_error_path_no_checkpoint_update: send chunk with wrong data size (decoded bytes != expected chunk_size for non-last chunk), verify HTTP 400 returned and checkpoint not updated
test_corrupt_checkpoint_handling: write garbage bytes to checkpoint.json, restart service, query /status; must return empty completed_chunks and completed_bytes=0, not crash

test_correct_mutex: upload 10 chunks with 4 workers, crash at CP_AFTER_PROGRESS_UPDATE for chunk 5; on resume, checkpoint must reflect exactly the chunks whose data was fsynced AND checkpoint written, not stale progress from a wrong-mutex write
anti_cheat: The hidden tests use different seeds to generate upload data and select crash points; the agent cannot predict which chunks or steps will be crashed. The checkpoint format is verified structurally (fields, types, sorting, no extra fields), so hard-coding a checkpoint or bypassing the writer fails. The crash-hook control endpoint is only in the test-controlled service instance; the agent cannot disable it. The service binary is checked for modification time (must be newer than source files, confirming recompilation). A hidden test sends invalid chunk data and corrupt checkpoints to verify error handling at runtime, not just by source inspection.
failure_modes:
- An agent might fix one bug but not all three: adding fsync without fixing the lock ordering still allows stale overwrites; making the write atomic without fsync still loses data on crash; moving the write inside the lock without making it atomic still allows truncated checkpoints on crash during write
- An agent might use checkpointMu instead of mu for the checkpoint write: single-worker tests pass, but multi-worker tests fail with stale overwrites because progress updates happen under mu, not checkpointMu
- An agent might fsync the data file but forget to fsync the checkpoint temp file before rename: the rename succeeds, the checkpoint appears correct, but after a crash the new checkpoint may be lost
- An agent might add a second mutex for checkpoint writes to avoid holding the progress mutex during IO: introduces a lock-ordering hazard; with 8 workers the harness's worst-case interleaving deadlocks
- An agent might forget to sort completed_chunks: the service works correctly, data is right, but the checkpoint format check fails because an external tool expects sorted indices
- An agent might not validate chunk data: invalid chunks update the checkpoint, causing wrong progress or data corruption
- An agent might not handle corrupt checkpoint.json on restart: the service crashes instead of starting fresh, failing recovery tests
shape: concurrency debugging; graded by a deterministic crash-and-resume harness
hidden_evaluation: The test harness in tests/ starts the service as a subprocess, enables the crash hook, uploads chunks concurrently via HTTP, and injects crashes at 40 controlled points (selected from seeded combinations of chunk index × processing step × worker count × file size). After each crash it restarts the service, resumes the upload, and compares the final data file and checkpoint against the known upload content. The harness also sends invalid chunk data, corrupts checkpoint.json, uploads chunks out of order, and checks error responses, checkpoint sorting, and corrupt-checkpoint recovery. The agent's own runs almost never hit the specific interleavings the harness tests; the harness uses the /control/crash-after endpoint to force them deterministically. The agent can discover and use the crash hook for single-worker testing but cannot reproduce the multi-worker interleavings or the specific invalid-input and corrupt-checkpoint scenarios the harness checks.

checks.requirement: checkpoint-format.md: 'Call fsync on the data file (ensure chunk data is durable on disk)' before updating the checkpoint
checks.assumed_instead: WriteAt returns no error, so the data is 'written' — no explicit fsync needed
checks.hidden_test_input: Crash at CP_AFTER_DATA_WRITE for chunk 3 of a 10-chunk upload with 4 workers; kernel has not flushed the page cache
checks.why_missed: The OS buffer cache hides the missing fsync in normal runs; only a true crash (or the harness simulating one) exposes it. The agent's single-worker crash tests catch this IF they test CP_AFTER_DATA_WRITE, but they might only test CP_AFTER_CHECKPOINT_WRITE

checks.requirement: checkpoint-format.md: 'Serialize the checkpoint to a temp file in the same directory … fsync the temp file … Rename the temp file to checkpoint.json'
checks.assumed_instead: os.WriteFile is convenient and works in practice; temp+fsync+rename is overkill
checks.hidden_test_input: Crash at CP_AFTER_TEMP_WRITE (temp file written, not fsynced, not renamed); checkpoint must be the previous valid version
checks.why_missed: Normal runs never crash during the brief write; only the harness's controlled crash reveals the truncation or partial state

checks.requirement: checkpoint-format.md: 'Acquire the upload mutex (mu) … Update the in-memory progress … [write checkpoint] … Release the upload mutex' — checkpoint write must be inside mu (the upload/progress mutex), not checkpointMu
checks.assumed_instead: Use checkpointMu for checkpoint writes (it's named for checkpoints) or snapshot under mu and write outside the lock to avoid holding the lock during IO
checks.hidden_test_input: 4 workers uploading chunks 0–9 concurrently; worker A snapshots {0,1,2} under mu or writes under checkpointMu, worker B snapshots and writes {0,1,2,3,4}, then worker A overwrites with stale {0,1,2}
checks.why_missed: Single-worker tests pass regardless of which mutex is used or whether the write is inside the lock; the stale overwrite is timing-dependent and only appears with multiple workers under the harness's deterministic interleaving

checks.requirement: checkpoint-format.md: 'Call fsync on the temp file' before rename — the rename must not outpace the temp file's durability
checks.assumed_instead: os.Rename is atomic at the filesystem level, so fsync of the temp file is unnecessary
checks.hidden_test_input: Crash after os.WriteFile(temp) but before fsync(temp); rename has not happened; on restart the temp file contents are lost and the old checkpoint remains
checks.why_missed: On Linux the temp file is in the page cache; only a crash or the harness reveals that the data never reached disk. The agent might test CP_AFTER_RENAME but not CP_AFTER_TEMP_FSYNC

checks.requirement: No deadlock: the single upload mutex (mu) must not be acquired in a nested or inconsistent order; do not introduce a second mutex for writes
checks.assumed_instead: Add a separate checkpoint mutex to serialise checkpoint writes independently, reducing lock hold time
checks.hidden_test_input: 8 workers uploading 20 chunks with uneven sizes; lock-ordering inversion between mu and the new checkpoint mutex causes deadlock under the harness's worst-case interleaving
checks.why_missed: Deadlocks only appear under specific interleavings; normal test runs may never trigger the lock inversion. The agent's multi-worker tests use random scheduling, not the harness's deterministic worst-case

checks.requirement: The checkpoint JSON format (upload_id, completed_chunks, completed_bytes, total_bytes, chunk_size, total_chunks) must not change — no extra fields, no renamed keys
checks.assumed_instead: Add a version field or restructure the JSON for clarity
checks.hidden_test_input: An external tool reads checkpoint.json expecting exactly the documented schema; a new field or renamed key breaks it
checks.why_missed: The agent's own tests check that required fields are present but may not check that NO extra fields exist

checks.requirement: The HTTP API (/upload/{id}/start, /chunk, /status, /complete) responses must keep the same shape — no extra fields
checks.assumed_instead: Add a checkpoint_sha field to the /status response for debugging
checks.hidden_test_input: A client parsing the /status response expects exactly the documented fields; extra fields break strict parsers
checks.why_missed: Extra fields don't break the agent's own curl tests but break the harness's response validation

checks.requirement: After crash and resume, completed_bytes must equal the exact sum of completed chunk sizes — never more (doubled) or less (lost)
checks.assumed_instead: Re-uploading a chunk that was already complete just overwrites the same offset; the byte count might be incremented again
checks.hidden_test_input: Crash after worker B writes checkpoint {0,1,2,3,4} but worker A overwrites with stale {0,1,2}; on resume, chunks 3 and 4 are re-uploaded and their bytes counted again
checks.why_missed: The data file ends up correct (WriteAt is idempotent) but the progress counter is wrong; only the harness checks the counter against the actual sum

checks.requirement: After a successful upload, no checkpoint.json.tmp file must remain in the upload directory
checks.assumed_instead: The temp file is overwritten on the next write, so leaving it is harmless
checks.hidden_test_input: An external cleanup script scans for .tmp files and alerts on any found; or a resume misreads the .tmp as the checkpoint
checks.why_missed: The agent's test_resume.sh doesn't check for leftover temp files; only the harness scans the directory

checks.requirement: Resumed upload must skip chunks already marked complete in the checkpoint, not re-process them
checks.assumed_instead: Re-processing a complete chunk is idempotent for the data, so skipping is just an optimisation
checks.hidden_test_input: A chunk whose data is already fsynced gets its WriteAt+Sync called again; the harness's write-tracker detects the redundant write
checks.why_missed: The data is correct either way; only the harness's write-tracker detects the redundant write

checks.requirement: checkpoint-format.md: 'completed_chunks must be a JSON array of integers sorted in ascending order'
checks.assumed_instead: Append chunks in completion order; the array has the right content, just not sorted — the service works fine either way
checks.hidden_test_input: Upload chunks out of order (indices 2, 0, 4, 1, 3 with 4 workers); read checkpoint.json and verify completed_chunks is [0,1,2,3,4], not [2,0,4,1,3]
checks.why_missed: No runtime error occurs with unsorted chunks; the service resumes correctly. Only an external reader or the harness's structural validation catches the ordering. The agent's own tests check field presence, not array ordering

checks.requirement: checkpoint-format.md: 'If the chunk data is invalid (decoded size does not match the expected chunk size, or base64 is unparseable), return HTTP 400 and do not update the checkpoint or write to the data file'
checks.assumed_instead: Process the chunk anyway; if the data is wrong, it overwrites the file at the right offset — the checkpoint is still updated
checks.hidden_test_input: Send a chunk with chunk_index=2 where the base64 decodes to 100 bytes but the expected chunk_size is 4096; verify HTTP 400 returned, checkpoint not updated, data file not modified
checks.why_missed: Normal uploads always send valid data; the agent's tests never send invalid chunks. No runtime error occurs if invalid data is written — the data file just has wrong bytes at that offset, which only the harness's byte-comparison catches

checks.requirement: checkpoint-format.md: 'On startup, if checkpoint.json exists but cannot be parsed as valid JSON, log a warning and treat the upload as having no completed chunks (completed_chunks=[], completed_bytes=0); do not crash'
checks.assumed_instead: Let json.Unmarshal panic or return a fatal error; or ignore the file silently and continue with whatever in-memory state exists
checks.hidden_test_input: Write 50 bytes of garbage to checkpoint.json, restart the service, query GET /upload/abc/status; verify response has completed_chunks=[] and completed_bytes=0, and the service does not crash
checks.why_missed: Normal runs never produce corrupt checkpoints; the agent doesn't test this case. The crash only manifests if the agent's own atomic-write fix has a bug that leaves a truncated file — which the agent might not catch if they don't test CP_DURING_CHECKPOINT_WRITE with multi-worker

preserved_behaviours.behaviour: POST /upload/{id}/start creates a new upload and returns {upload_id, completed_chunks, total_chunks} with exactly those fields
POST /upload/{id}/chunk processes a chunk and returns {status: ok, completed_chunks: [...]} with exactly those fields
GET /upload/{id}/status returns {upload_id, completed_chunks, completed_bytes, total_bytes, total_chunks} with exactly those fields
POST /upload/{id}/complete returns {status: ok, total_bytes} with exactly those fields

Checkpoint JSON has exactly the fields: upload_id (string), completed_chunks (array of int, sorted ascending), completed_bytes (int), total_bytes (int), chunk_size (int), total_chunks (int) — no extra fields
preserved_behaviours.hidden_test_input: Read checkpoint.json after any upload state

ground_truth: The test harness in tests/harness.py generates deterministic upload data from a seed (using hash-based chunk content), starts the Go service with ENABLE_CRASH_HOOK=1, uses the /control/crash-after endpoint to inject crashes at specific numbered crash points, uploads chunks concurrently via HTTP, waits for the service to exit(99), restarts it, queries /status for completed chunks, uploads the remainder, and compares the final data file byte-for-byte against the generated original. Expected checkpoint contents are computed from the set of chunks known to have been fully processed (data fsynced + checkpoint written + renamed) before the crash, determined by the crash point number and the upload state. The harness also: (a) sends invalid chunk data (wrong decoded size) and checks for HTTP 400 and no checkpoint update; (b) corrupts checkpoint.json and checks graceful recovery; (c) uploads chunks out of order and checks completed_chunks is sorted ascending; (d) validates response shapes have no extra fields. The harness is deterministic: same seed produces same data, same crash point, same interleaving, same expected resume state.

stated_facts.fact: Chunk data must be fsynced to disk before the checkpoint is updated to include that chunk
stated_facts.why: Running the service cannot demonstrate durability; the OS buffer cache makes unfsynced writes appear successful until a crash removes them

stated_facts.fact: The checkpoint must be written to a temp file in the same directory, fsynced, then atomically renamed
stated_facts.why: A crash during os.WriteFile can leave a truncated file; this is invisible in normal runs because WriteFile typically completes in microseconds

stated_facts.fact: The checkpoint write must occur while holding the upload mutex (mu), not the checkpoint read mutex (checkpointMu)
stated_facts.why: The stale-overwrite race is timing-dependent and almost never manifests in uncontrolled runs; only a deterministic scheduler or crash hook can reliably expose it. Single-worker runs cannot distinguish correct-mutex from wrong-mutex usage

stated_facts.fact: Invalid chunk data (decoded size mismatch or unparseable base64) must not update the checkpoint or write to the data file; return HTTP 400
stated_facts.why: Normal uploads always send valid data, so the practice data and test_resume.sh never exercise this path; the agent cannot observe the failure without deliberately sending invalid data

stated_facts.fact: On startup, if checkpoint.json exists but is not valid JSON, the service must treat the upload as having no completed chunks rather than crashing
stated_facts.why: A corrupt checkpoint only arises from a crash during a non-atomic write — exactly the bug being fixed. The practice data never has a corrupt checkpoint, so the agent cannot observe this path without manually corrupting the file

dial: Number of injected crash points that must resume exactly. Fair range 20–100; chosen value 40 (6 crash points per chunk × ~7 chunks average across the test scenarios). Each crash point is a separate parameterised test case; all 40 must pass.
quirk_matrix: {"dimensions": {"crash_point": ["between_chunks", "after_data_write_before_fsync", "after_fsync_before_progress", "after_progress_before_checkpoint", "after_temp_write_before_fsync", "after_temp_fsync_before_rename", "after_rename"], "workers": ["1", "4", "8_uneven"], "file_size": ["small_5chunks", "medium_10chunks", "many_20chunks"], "input_validity": ["valid", "invalid_size", "invalid_base64"], "checkpoint_state": ["valid", "corrupt_json", "absent"]}, "mix": "About 30% easy cells (1 worker, small file, between_chunks crash, valid input, valid checkpoint); the rest stress concurrent writers, mid-operation crashes, uneven last-chunk boundaries, invalid inputs, and corrupt checkpoints"}
public_tests: A shell script at /app/test_resume.sh that starts the service, uploads a 5-chunk file with 2 workers, kills the service after chunk 2 completes (quiet point between chunks), restarts, resumes, and verifies the final data. This covers ~30% of the checked scenarios: basic resume, checkpoint reading, and status API. It does not crash during a write, does not test concurrent-worker races, does not verify fsync ordering, does not send invalid data, does not corrupt the checkpoint, and does not check completed_chunks sorting.
anti_cheese: The hidden crash-point harness uses seeded random crash points unknown to the agent; hard-coding checkpoint contents for the practice data fails on the graded seeds. The checkpoint format is validated structurally (required JSON fields, types, no extra fields, completed_chunks sorted ascending), so bypassing the writer or writing a static file fails. The service binary's mtime must be newer than the source files, confirming the agent recompiled after editing. A hidden test sends invalid chunk data and corrupt checkpoints at runtime (not just source scanning) to verify error handling. A hidden test verifies the /control/ endpoint and ENABLE_CRASH_HOOK still work in the submitted binary, ensuring the agent didn't disable the hook. A hidden test removes forbidden helper binaries from PATH during grading.
graded_instances: The graded instances use 5 different seeds (100–104) to generate upload data (varying total_bytes from 20KiB to 160KiB, chunk_size from 4096 to 8192) and select crash points. Each seed produces a different set of 40 crash-point test cases plus 5 non-crash test cases (invalid input, corrupt checkpoint, out-of-order upload, format check, API check). The harness is deterministic: same seed + same crash point = same data + same interleaving + same expected resume state. A determinism self-check runs the same seed twice and asserts byte-identical upload data and identical crash-point numbering.
self_check_gap: A fix that passes test_resume.sh (quiet-point crash) and even single-worker crash tests at every crash point can still fail on: (1) multi-worker interleaving — the agent cannot control which goroutine runs when the crash hook fires, so the stale-overwrite race (wrong mutex or write outside lock) may not manifest in the agent's runs but does in the harness's deterministic schedule; (2) invalid chunk data — the agent's tests never send invalid data, so missing validation produces no runtime signal; (3) corrupt checkpoint — the agent's runs never produce a corrupt checkpoint, so missing graceful recovery produces no runtime signal; (4) unsorted completed_chunks — the service works correctly with unsorted chunks, so only the harness's structural validation catches it. The practice set (test_resume.sh + source code + checkpoint-format.md) determines the right answer because every rule is stated in the document and every bug is visible in the source, but the agent cannot fully verify their implementation matches every rule without the harness's controlled interleaving, invalid-input injection, and structural format checks.

contract: POST /upload/{id}/start body={total_bytes:int, chunk_size:int} → {upload_id:string, completed_chunks:[int], total_chunks:int} (exactly these fields)
POST /upload/{id}/chunk body={chunk_index:int, data:base64} → {status:"ok", completed_chunks:[int]} (exactly these fields) on success; HTTP 400 with {error:string} on invalid data
GET /upload/{id}/status → {upload_id:string, completed_chunks:[int], completed_bytes:int, total_bytes:int, total_chunks:int} (exactly these fields)

Checkpoint file: DIR/uploads/{id}/checkpoint.json with exactly the fields {upload_id:string, completed_chunks:[int sorted ascending], completed_bytes:int, total_bytes:int, chunk_size:int, total_chunks:int}
On crash (exit code 99 from crash hook, or SIGKILL), the service must leave the checkpoint in a valid state (valid JSON or absent; never truncated; no .tmp file treated as checkpoint)

On resume (restart with existing data dir), the service reads checkpoint.json; if valid JSON, populates completed_chunks and completed_bytes from it; if invalid JSON or absent, treats as empty progress (completed_chunks=[], completed_bytes=0)

Chunk processing order: (1) validate chunk data (decoded size == expected chunk_size for non-last chunk, or <= remaining bytes for last chunk; base64 parseable); (2) WriteAt to data file; (3) fsync data file; (4) acquire mu; (5) update completedChunks and completedBytes; (6) sort completedChunks ascending; (7) write checkpoint atomically (temp + fsync + rename) inside mu; (8) release mu
Precedence: checkpoint-format.md specification wins over any observed behavior of the current code or comments in the source

invisible_traps.trap: Not validating chunk data before writing: an invalid chunk (wrong decoded size) is written to the data file at the right offset, the checkpoint is updated, the /chunk endpoint returns 200 OK — everything looks fine until the harness byte-compares the final data file and finds wrong bytes at that offset
invisible_traps.stated_in: checkpoint-format.md: 'If the chunk data is invalid (decoded size does not match the expected chunk size, or base64 is unparseable), return HTTP 400 and do not update the checkpoint or write to the data file'

invisible_traps.trap: Crashing on corrupt checkpoint.json during restart: readCheckpoint calls json.Unmarshal which panics or returns a fatal error on garbage input — the service never starts, and the harness's restart-and-resume step fails with a non-99 exit code
invisible_traps.stated_in: checkpoint-format.md: 'On startup, if checkpoint.json exists but cannot be parsed as valid JSON, log a warning and treat the upload as having no completed chunks; do not crash'

invisible_traps.trap: Adding a second mutex for checkpoint writes to avoid holding mu during IO: introduces a lock-ordering hazard; with 8 workers the harness's worst-case interleaving deadlocks — no error message, just a timeout
invisible_traps.stated_in: checkpoint-format.md: 'Acquire the upload mutex' (singular) for the entire sequence; using two locks is not specified

seed_card:
topic: A Go upload service's multi-threaded checkpoint writer sometimes resumes with lost or doubled progress
  after a crash; find and fix the race.
shape: concurrency debugging; graded by a deterministic crash-and-resume harness
agent_cannot_verify: The race needs a specific interleaving; the agent's runs rarely hit it. The hidden
  harness injects crashes at controlled points with a deterministic scheduler hook.
dial: number of injected crash points that must resume exactly; fair range 20-100.
quirk_matrix:
  crash point:
  - between chunks
  - during a write
  - between write and rename
  workers:
  - '1'
  - '4'
  - 8 with uneven chunk sizes
  file size:
  - small
  - medium
  - many chunks
  mix: about 30% easy cells
self_check_gap: a fix that passes the practice harness at its default scheduling can still lose bytes
  at a crash point between two writes the practice run never hits; the checkpoint format document states
  the write order and the harness exposes every crash point
answer_source: stated
reference_access: none
quirk_evidence:
- quirk: crash point
  evidence: docs/checkpoint-format.md describes the write order; the service source shows every step
- quirk: workers
  evidence: the service source and README state the worker pool
- quirk: file size
  evidence: README states the chunk size and the last-chunk rule
public_tests: 'about 30%: a visible resume test with a crash at a quiet point'
anti_cheese: the deterministic crash-point harness on hidden seeds AND an unchanged checkpoint format
ground_truth: the harness in tests/ drives the service through a scheduler hook and checks the resumed
  byte count against the uploaded data.
checks:
- checkpoint written only after the chunk is durable (fsync order)
- atomic rename of the checkpoint file
- a worker that finishes a chunk after another worker's checkpoint
- no deadlock under the harness's worst interleaving
- the upload API and checkpoint format unchanged
knobs:
- knob: preservation constraints
  fairness: README states the checkpoint format other tools read
- knob: varied hidden draws
  fairness: crash points drawn from several seeds; each a stated recovery requirement
must_keep:
- checkpoint file format
- HTTP upload API
environment: golang image with the service source (~600 lines) and go.mod vendored; no network.
out_of_bounds:
- races only reachable with real timing
- OS-specific durability guarantees not stated
precheck:
- confirm the harness reproduces the bug deterministically on the unfixed code
crux: The three main bugs (fsync, atomic write, mutex) are all stated in checkpoint-format.md and a careful agent fixes them. The difficulty comes from four invisible traps that produce no runtime signal: (1) using the wrong mutex (checkpointMu instead of mu) — passes all single-worker tests, fails multi-worker; (2) not sorting completed_chunks — service works perfectly, only structural validation catches it; (3) not validating chunk data — invalid data is silently written, only byte-comparison catches it; (4) crashing on corrupt checkpoint — only triggers if the agent's own atomic-write fix has a residual bug or the harness corrupts the file deliberately. A strong agent that reads checkpoint-format.md line by line and tests each rule gets all of them; one that fixes the three obvious bugs and runs test_resume.sh gets 3-4 of 13 checks wrong.
